Internal source backport for GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm

This private package starts from the registry-verified braces 3.0.3 source and
retains its MIT license and fill-range 7.1.1 dependency. It is maintained by this
repository; it is not a published upstream release or an external third-party
fork. The original package/version/advisory are recorded in package.json.

The parser rejects more than 127 brace/parenthesis containers before recursive
cleanup. An iterative preflight bounds all compile/expand/stringify child walks
to 128 edges and 65536 visits; child cycles and malformed array-valued text are
rejected with SyntaxError / ERR_BRACES_COMPLEXITY. Options cannot raise these
structural bounds. Expansion follows the active traversal, not foreign parent
metadata, so parent-pointer cycles cannot trap the walker or import queues.

The 10000-character hard cap remains active for NaN/Infinity maxLength values.
AST counters must be numeric values; NaN counters generated by the original
parser are retained. Coercing range/regex options accept primitives, not
nested object/array values. The short-string fast path does not coerce foreign
AST length metadata. These controls cover passive JSON payloads as well as
deeply nested pattern strings.

This does not claim a general sandbox for getters/proxies, a bound on regex
execution time, or a bound on expansion cardinality. Existing rangeLimit and
ordinary expansion semantics remain in place. Supported build/lint glob use
and the site's CSS output must be verified before adoption.

Independent local source review was completed on 2026-10-08 for the eight
runtime modules recorded in PATCH-INTEGRITY.json. It included 412164 API
comparisons, boundary/AST/option attacks, and build/lint consumer compatibility.
Actual installed routing, independent mapping review, and the full project
checks are required before this package is published with the application.

Upstream tracking and maintenance

UPSTREAM.json retains the vulnerable upstream identity, reviewed advisory,
registry tarball integrity, and SHA-256 hashes of the original source files.
The advisory remains open upstream; a zero registry audit after replacement
does not mean the official braces 3.0.3 release has become safe. This repository
takes responsibility for the modified code. Registry signatures cover external
dependencies, not this private package's locally maintained source.

For each dependency refresh or release, check the advisory and official braces
release history. Prefer a reviewed maintainer-published fix when available;
remove this replacement only after testing all installed consumer paths. Do
not substitute an unreviewed external fork or raise the structural bounds.

Every local code change requires independent source review, adversarial and
baseline API tests, installed graph verification, CSS/glob/watcher/lint checks,
full audits, package signature verification, and the normal project checks.
Keep the MIT license and upstream identity when updating the source baseline.
Document the reviewed implementation in the release evidence. Expansion
cardinality, rangeLimit overrides, and arbitrary executable getters/proxies
remain outside this recursion-advisory mitigation; assess new advisories on
their merits rather than treating this package as exempt from review.
